newsitem.title: UK: Booker up after figures, trading statement.
newsitem.headline: Booker up after figures, trading statement.

text.p: Shares in Booker Plc were up 10-1/2p or three percent to 347-1/2 by 0940 GMT after the food manufacturer and distribution group reported sharply lower pre-tax profits due to large exceptional charges.
But steady sales growth figures and a confident trading statement helped push the shares higher, dealers and market makers said.
"The figures were nothing to get excited about but the company said it expects its reorganisation strategy to payoff in the next couple of years," one market maker said.
"Booker has suffered with the rest of the food sector the past few months so was due for a bounce."
As of the close on Monday, March 24, Booker shares had underperformed the FTSE All Share index by around 20 percent over the past six months, according to data from Reuters Securities 3000.

The company reported 1996 pre-tax, pre-exceptional profits of 101.9 million stg versus 100.6 million a year ago. After exceptionals the pre-tax figure slumped to 13.0 million stg compared with 82.8 million stg.

Booker also said it had seen five to six percent like-for like sales growth in its cash-and-carry-business since its year ended December 28. About two thirds of the company's overall profits come from cash-and-carry.

Booker said a reorganisation of the company's businesses, which has included the disposal of non-core divisions, would proceed this year and would result in a stronger company performance in the future.
"In 1998 most of these major tasks will be completed and we anticipate significant benefits will come through for our shareholders," the company said in a statement.
